frozen_claim: A standard neuronal-avalanche power-law pipeline is a diagnostic detector of network criticality rather than a high-false-positive measurement pipeline.

observable.name: criticality_false_positive_rate
observable.definition: False-positive rate (FPR) of a fully validated avalanche power-law + crackling-relation pipeline on a matched non-critical control, alongside the true-positive rate (TPR) on a critical positive control, scanned across sample size. A condition is called 'critical' only if BOTH tests pass: (a) a discrete power-law fit — Hurwitz-zeta MLE of the exponent over a grid, KS-minimised lower cutoff x_min selected separately for avalanche size and duration, accepted when the KS distance is below the asymptotic 5% threshold 1.36/sqrt(n_tail); and (b) the crackling relation — the slope of log-binned <S>(T) within 20% of the predicted (alpha-1)/(tau-1). An n_aval >= 150 admissibility gate applies. FPR = pass-rate ('critical' calls) on the matched subcritical control; TPR = pass-rate on the critical positive control. Reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals over 120 trials per condition per sample size.

model.generative: Galton-Watson branching avalanches with Poisson offspring mean m; each avalanche yields a (size, duration) pair. Critical at m=1.0; the matched non-critical control is subcritical at m=0.9. No real neural recordings are used; the test is a synthetic false-positive probe of the measurement pipeline.
model.config: offspring=Poisson(m*cur), avalanche size cap=50000; sample sizes scanned n_aval = 300, 500, 800, 1500, 2500, 4000; 120 trials per condition per sample size; pipeline parameters: exponent grid 1.05..4.00 step 0.01, x_min over 1..8, KS threshold 1.36/sqrt(n_tail), crackling log-bins=12, crackling band 20%, admissibility n_aval>=150.
model.controls: matched subcritical (m=0.9) negative control vs critical (m=1.0) positive control, both passed through the identical pipeline.

thresholds.ci: Wilson 95% over 120 trials per condition per sample size
thresholds.decision_rule: The thesis (PRO: pipeline is a diagnostic detector) is ACCEPTED only if the critical positive control passes AND the matched non-critical control's FPR is below the 0.05 diagnostic target at literature-typical sample sizes AND the exponent/crackling relation separates critical from non-critical. The registered falsifier FIRES (thesis rejected) if FPR >= 0.20 on a matched non-critical control that also passes both the power-law and crackling tests.

nulls: matched_subcritical_branching (m=0.9): a non-critical process with the same generative family; a genuine diagnostic detector should call it 'critical' at a rate below the 0.05 target, while a high-false-positive pipeline does not.
critical positive control (m=1.0) required to pass for a valid (non-DRAW) outcome.
failure_modes: Synthetic Galton-Watson branching, not real cortical recordings — the decisive external-validity limitation: this cannot establish that real avalanche data are misdiagnosed, only that the pipeline has a high false-positive rate on a matched synthetic subcritical control.

A single matched subcritical surrogate (Poisson offspring, m=0.9) and a single fixed detection/fitting pipeline are used; the registered comparator ladder also lists subsampled-critical and AR(1)/shot-noise surrogates, which are NOT part of this decisive repro.
More elaborate detection schemes (multi-channel binning, explicit model comparison against alternatives) were not tested, so the result does not show every literature pipeline behaves identically.

At very large n the positive-control TPR itself begins to erode (0.900 at n=4000) because the KS-minimised x_min trims short avalanches intrinsic to the critical distribution — a separate finite-size/estimator tension, not part of the headline FPR claim.
accepted_evidence_criteria: The registered falsifier is met (thesis rejected) if, at literature-typical sample sizes, the matched subcritical control passes both the power-law and crackling tests with FPR >= 0.20 while the critical positive control passes — established here at n_aval = 300/500/800 with FPR 0.39-0.47 (lower CI above 0.20 at every size) and TPR 0.82-0.98.
rejected_evidence_criteria: The thesis (PRO) would be upheld if the critical positive control passes AND the matched subcritical control's FPR falls below the 0.05 diagnostic target at literature-typical sample sizes; in the scan this only occurs at n_aval >= 2500 (FPR 0.042), an order of magnitude above typical avalanche counts, so the thesis is not upheld in its registered regime.
